questionText:
Choose the correct choice(s) regarding the following propositional logic assertion $S$:

$$S : ((P \wedge Q) \rightarrow R) \rightarrow ((P \wedge Q) \rightarrow (Q \rightarrow R))$$
options: $S$ is neither a tautology nor a contradiction.
The antecedent of $S$ is logically equivalent to the consequent of $S$.
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the Antecedent and Consequent of $S$
The given assertion $S$ is in the form of an implication $A ightarrow B$, where:
• Antecedent $A = ((P \wedge Q) ightarrow R)$
• Consequent $B = ((P \wedge Q) ightarrow (Q ightarrow R))$

Step 2: Simplify the Consequent ($B$)
Using logical equivalences ($X ightarrow Y \equiv eg X \vee Y$):
$B \equiv eg (P \wedge Q) \vee (Q ightarrow R)$
$B \equiv ( eg P \vee eg Q) \vee ( eg Q \vee R)$
Applying associativity and idempotence of OR ($ \vee$):
$B \equiv eg P \vee eg Q \vee R$
$B \equiv eg (P \wedge Q) \vee R$
$B \equiv (P \wedge Q) ightarrow R$

Step 3: Evaluate Statement Equivalence and Tautology
Since $B \equiv (P \wedge Q) ightarrow R$, we have $A \equiv B$. Thus, the antecedent of $S$ is logically equivalent to the consequent of $S$. This makes option (D) correct.

Since $A \equiv B$, the assertion $S: A ightarrow B$ becomes $A ightarrow A$, which is always True (a Tautology). This makes option (B) correct.
